function.name: locate_tallest_mountains
function.description: Find the tallest mountains within a specified radius of a location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city from which to calculate distance.

radius.description: The radius within which to find mountains, measured in kilometers. This is a float type value.

amount.description: The number of mountains to find, listed from tallest to smallest.

function.name: calculate_electric_field
function.description: Calculate the electric field produced by a charge at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

distance.description: Distance from the charge in meters where the field is being measured. This is a float type value.

permitivity.description: Permitivity of the space where field is being calculated, default is for vacuum. This is a float type value.

function.name: calculate_genotype_frequency

message.content:
**Proteins that are commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often serve as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** such as β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ion channels**: voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv), calcium channel (Cav), ligand‑gated NMDA receptor
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases**: EGFR, HER2
• **Integrins** (αβ heterodimers, e.g., α5β1)
• **Cadherins** (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels, e.g., Cx43)
• **Tetraspanins** (CD9, CD81) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via electrostatic or lipid‑anchor interactions; often link to the cytoskeleton or signaling complexes. | • **Ankyrin‑R** (links integral proteins to spectrin)
• **Spectrin** (provides membrane skeleton)
• **Actin‑binding proteins**: ezrin, radixin, moesin (ERM family)
• **Src family kinases** (e.g., Src, Fyn) – often palmitoylated or myristoylated for membrane attachment
• **GAPs and GEFs** that regulate small GTPases at the membrane (e.g., p120‑RasGAP)
• **Adaptor proteins**: Grb2, Shc, LAT (link receptors to downstream pathways) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., GPI anchors) and reside on the outer leaflet. | • **GPI‑anchored proteins**: CD59, CD55 (complement regulators)
• **Prion protein (PrP^C)** (GPI‑anchored, involved in cell signaling)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** that are GPI‑anchored (e.g., some growth factor receptors) | | **Other specialized proteins** | Serve unique roles such as cell–cell communication or mechanical support. | • **Desmosomal cadherins** (desmoglein, desmocollin)
• **Hemidesmosomal proteins** (integrin α6β4, BPAG1)
• **Synaptic vesicle proteins** (synaptophysin, SNAP‑25) – localized to presynaptic membranes | ### How to use this list - **Research**: If you’re studying a particular cell type, look up the specific isoforms expressed (e.g., neuronal cells express Nav1.6, Cav2.1). - **Drug targeting**: Many drugs target plasma‑membrane proteins (e.g., β‑blockers target β‑adrenergic GPCRs, statins target HMG‑CoA reductase on the membrane). - **Diagnostics**: Surface markers (e.g., CD antigens) are used in flow cytometry to identify cell populations. Feel free to ask for more details on any specific protein family or for a curated list for a particular cell type!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They want a list of proteins found in the plasma membrane. We can provide a general answer: types of proteins: integral membrane proteins (e.g., ion channels, transporters, receptors), peripheral membrane proteins (e.g., cytoskeletal proteins, signaling proteins). Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors, integrins, cadherins, connexins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins like ankyrin, spectrin, actin-binding proteins. Provide a concise but informative answer. No function calls needed.
